verdict.reasoning: Patient: "a weird swelling on my elbow... about a week ago" and later confirms "It's the left elbow."
Same as cc-001: swelling on the left elbow, noticed "about a week ago."
Patient: "It's not painful at all. I feel fine, but it's just a bit weird to see..."
Patient: "it's slightly warm" and later confirms when asked: "It's a bit warm?" / Doctor: "Yes, it's a bit warmer."
Patient: "I kind of feel like it's a bit fluid inside" and on palpation: "where the swelling is? It's a bit. Yeah, it feels a bit fluid."
Patient: "I think I have something like osteoarthritis" and later confirms diagnosis: Doctor: "Has anyone ever told you that?..." Patient: "Yes, a few years ago." Doctor clarifies it was a GP.
Doctor: "And do you, are you on any medication on a regular basis?" Patient: "No, no."
Doctor: "I would take ibuprofen regularly... That's 400 milligrams, three times a day. And you should take that after food, not an empty stomach."
Patient: "I'm allergic to. To peanuts. That's pretty much all I had to say about my medical history."
Doctor: "Are you allergic to any medication?" Patient: "No, not that I know of."

Doctor asks about family rheumatologic disease; Patient: "No. Well, I... think I have something like osteoarthritis... but in my family, I'm not sure." This indicates he does not report a family history of rheumatologic disease.
Doctor: "in terms of your job, do you do anything physical?" Patient: "Not really, no. I just, you know, sit at the desk."
Patient: "I do, I do do some sports. I run regularly. Like two, three times a week."
Doctor: "This seems like what we call the bursitis. Okay. So that's an inflammation of one of the fluid sacs around the joint" after discussing warm, swollen, fluid-feeling elbow.
Doctor: "I would take ibuprofen regularly... That's 400 milligrams, three times a day. And you should take that after food, not an empty stomach."
Doctor: "get some blood tests done... check for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies... and also check for things like gout as well."
Doctor: "we're going to arrange some blood test forms to be sent out to your house"

Doctor: "results will come back to us after about five, six days" and "we can arrange a follow up appointment... after you've had the blood test done"; also earlier: "we're looking at maybe six days."

Doctor explains septic arthritis warning signs: "if the elbow was to become very red, very painful, and the redness was to spread... then you need to get on the phone or have a video appointment with one of us as soon as possible because that would be an emergency."
From exam discussion: Patient/doctor confirm swelling, warmth, and fluid feel: "It's a bit warm?" / "Yes..." and "where the swelling is? It's a bit. Yeah, it feels a bit fluid."
Doctor: "I noticed the skin was a bit dry on the tip of the elbow. Do you have dry skin anywhere else..." Patient: "No" and denies eczema, implying no other dermatologic findings mentioned.
